package_info.why_malicious: A compromised version of the polyfill.io JavaScript library was used to inject malicious code into the Internet Archive website, resulting in site defacement and potentially enabling further attacks such as credential theft or data exfiltration. The malicious code executed in users' browsers, violating the trust model of third-party libraries and enabling unauthorized modification of site content.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (client-side, when user visits the site)
execution_context.file_location: polyfill.io JavaScript library loaded via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script> (or similar)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code modifies the DOM to overwrite the website's content with a defacement message, resulting in visible site defacement for all visitors.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Third-party JavaScript libraries should not modify the main page content or display defacement messages. Such behavior is indicative of a supply chain attack or library compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal polyfill libraries provide compatibility shims and do not alter page content or perform defacement. The actual behavior is unauthorized DOM manipulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate site banners or notifications may update the DOM, but not via a polyfill library and not to display defacement messages.
key_indicators: DOM overwrite via document.body.innerHTML or document.write
Defacement message injected from a third-party library
Unexpected modification of site content by a polyfill

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is served via the compromised polyfill.io CDN and loaded by the Internet Archive website.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in the browser of every site visitor.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the user's browser, overwriting the DOM to display a defacement message.
attack_chain.leads_to: Site defacement visible to all visitors; potential for further attacks (e.g., credential theft, data exfiltration) if additional payloads are present.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected DOM manipulation by third-party JavaScript libraries
Defacement messages injected into page content at runtime
Polyfill or utility libraries performing actions outside their intended scope
file_indicators: polyfill.min.js loaded from untrusted or compromised CDN
Inline scripts or external scripts modifying document.body.innerHTML or document.write with defacement content
network_indicators: Requests to compromised polyfill.io CDN endpoints
Unusual script loads from third-party domains not previously used by the site
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected DOM changes initiated by third-party scripts, especially those loaded from polyfill.io or similar CDNs. Alert on any script that overwrites the main content of the page or injects defacement messages. Track changes in the content of externally loaded JavaScript libraries and compare against known-good hashes. Block or alert on polyfill.io CDN usage if the domain is known to be compromised.
